question: Why did the authors pick sinusoidal positional encodings, and what happened when they tried learned positional embeddings?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §3.5 Positional Encoding; AIAYN §6.2 Model Variations; AIAYN §3.4 Embeddings and Softmax; AIAYN §5.4 Regularization.
drafts: The authors chose sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesized that the sinusoid function would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PE_{pos+k} can be represented as a linear function of PE_{pos}, and because it may enable extrapolation to sequence lengths longer than those seen during training [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. They also experimented with learned positional embeddings and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results, with the learned version yielding a dev perplexity of 4.92 and BLEU of 25.7, essentially the same as the base model [AIAYN:3.5:c020][AIAYN:T3:r08][AIAYN:6.2:c031].

The authors selected sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesized the function would let the model easily learn to attend by relative positions and might allow extrapolation to longer sequence lengths [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. They also tried learned positional embeddings and observed nearly identical results to the sinusoidal version, with the learned variant yielding a dev perplexity of 4.92 and BLEU of 25.7, matching the base model’s performance [AIAYN:3.5:c020][AIAYN:6.2:c031].
